Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Compared with the input image, is there visible progress toward closing the same woman's jacket, when corresponding evidence of its front closure can be compared?
node.criteria: Pass: comparable visible evidence shows the jacket has moved toward closure, but the edited jacket is not fully closed. Fail: comparable visible evidence establishes no progress toward closure. Unknown: pose, occlusion, drape, or other differences prevent a reliable comparison of the actual closure; an open-looking edited silhouette alone is not evidence of no progress.
node.binding: Compare the same woman's pink jacket in the source and edited images, focusing on corresponding visible evidence of the actual front closure. Count only progress toward closure, not unrelated edits; do not infer no progress from an uncomparable view.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows the woman mostly facing forward, while in the edited image she is turned sideways and the jacket front is obscured by its drape. The actual front closure cannot be reliably compared, so progress toward closing it is not established.

fulfillment: The node’s uncertainty is defensible: the edited jacket’s front closure is obscured by its drape and the subject’s changed pose, so do not force a “yes” from the reference label or treat the visible pink fabric as proof of closure. The aggregate mismatch is a signal to investigate whether the binding and evidence criteria are too narrow or poorly operationalized, not atomic ground truth. Clarify the binding to assess the jacket’s actual front closure and whether any opening remains, while distinguishing visible closure evidence from pose, drape, and unrelated appearance changes. Keep the progress check tied to comparable evidence of the requested closure change; do not infer progress merely from the changed pose. Preserve unknown when the closure cannot be seen reliably. The trace is valid uncertainty, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated; avoid changing routing or weakening the rubric just to match the reference.
